pairs.source_text: Africam Graeci Libyam appellavere et mare ante eam Libycum.
pairs.question: Quo nomine Africa a Graecis appellata esse a Plinio dicitur?
pairs.question_en: By what name does Pliny say Africa was called by the Greeks?
pairs.derivation: Opening fact of the book: the Greek name for Africa is Libya. Anchored to Africa + the Greeks; single named answer supported verbatim by Africam Graeci Libyam appellavere. Nominativus cum infinitivo (Africa appellata esse) governed by dicitur; closed-book because Libya as the Greek term for Africa is a commonplace of ancient geography.

pairs.source_text: multo tamen magis Autololum gente, per quam iter est ad montem Africae vel fabulosissimum Atlantem.
pairs.question: Quem montem Plinius 'montem Africae vel fabulosissimum' nominat?
pairs.question_en: Which mountain does Pliny call 'the mountain of Africa, and the most fabulous'?
pairs.derivation: Identifies Atlas as the iconic mountain of Africa. Single named-mountain answer supported verbatim by montem Africae vel fabulosissimum Atlantem; nominat takes the double accusative (quem montem ... Atlantem). Closed-book: Mount Atlas is among the best-known landmarks of ancient geography.

pairs.source_text: ita se findente Nilo, ut triquetram terrae figuram efficiat, ideoque multi Graecae litterae vocabulo Delta appellavere Aegyptum.
pairs.question: Quo Graecae litterae vocabulo multi Aegyptum appellaverunt, ob triquetram figuram quam Nilus se findens efficit, secundum Plinium?
pairs.question_en: By the name of which Greek letter did many call Egypt, on account of the triangular shape that the Nile forms by splitting, according to Pliny?
pairs.answer_en: By the name of the letter Delta.
pairs.derivation: Egypt named 'Delta' from the Greek letter because the Nile, splitting, makes a triangular shape. Anchored to Egypt + the Nile; single answer supported verbatim by Graecae litterae vocabulo Delta appellavere Aegyptum. Closed-book and iconic (the Nile Delta).

pairs.source_text: auctus per puteos mensurae notis deprehenduntur. iustum incrementum est cubitorum XVI.
pairs.question: Quot cubitorum esse iustum Nili incrementum Plinius tradit?
pairs.question_en: Of how many cubits does Pliny say the proper rise of the Nile is?
pairs.derivation: The famous ideal flood-height of the Nile, sixteen cubits. Anchored to the Nile; single number answer supported verbatim by iustum incrementum est cubitorum XVI. Indirect statement (incrementum esse) governed by tradit; closed-book (the Nilometer's sixteen cubits).

pairs.source_text: inde LXII p. abest Memphis, quondam arx Aegypti regum.
pairs.question: Quod oppidum Aegypti quondam arx regum fuisse a Plinio dicitur?
pairs.question_en: Which Egyptian town does Pliny say was once the citadel of the kings?
pairs.derivation: Memphis as the ancient royal seat of Egypt. Anchored to Egypt + its kings; single-name answer supported verbatim by Memphis, quondam arx Aegypti regum. Nominativus cum infinitivo (oppidum ... arx fuisse) governed by dicitur; closed-book and recognizable.

pairs.source_text: Diospolis Magna, eadem Thebe portarum centum nobilis fama.
pairs.question: Quae urbs Aegypti, eadem Diospolis Magna, centum portarum fama nobilis est secundum Plinium?
pairs.question_en: Which Egyptian city, also called Diospolis Magna, is famed for its hundred gates, according to Pliny?
pairs.derivation: The hundred-gated Thebes (Diospolis Magna). Anchored to Egypt + the alternate name Diospolis Magna; single-name answer supported verbatim by Thebe portarum centum nobilis fama. Closed-book: the hekatompylos Thebes is a Homeric commonplace.

pairs.source_text: Sed iure laudetur in litore Aegyptii maris Alexandria, a Magno Alexandro condita in Africae parte ab ostio Canopico XII p. iuxta Mareotim lacum, qui locus antea Rhacotes nominabatur.
pairs.question: A quo Alexandria in Aegypto condita esse a Plinio traditur?
pairs.question_en: By whom does Pliny say Alexandria in Egypt was founded?
pairs.derivation: Founder fact: Alexander the Great founded Alexandria. Anchored to the city; single named-founder answer (ablative of agent) supported verbatim by Alexandria, a Magno Alexandro condita. Nominativus cum infinitivo governed by traditur; closed-book and iconic.

pairs.source_text: altera iuncta ponte Alexandriae, colonia Caesaris dictatoris, Pharos, quondam diei navigatione distans ab Aegypto, nunc e turri nocturnis ignibus cursum navium regens.
pairs.question: Quae insula apud Alexandriam e turri nocturnis ignibus cursum navium regere a Plinio dicitur?
pairs.question_en: Which island by Alexandria does Pliny say guides ships' course from a tower by nighttime fires?
pairs.derivation: The lighthouse island of Pharos at Alexandria. Anchored to Alexandria; single-name answer supported verbatim by Pharos ... e turri nocturnis ignibus cursum navium regens. Nominativus cum infinitivo governed by dicitur; closed-book (the Pharos, one of the Seven Wonders).

pairs.source_text: ac magis etiamnum meridiana Babylonia, eadem Mesopotamia inter Euphraten et Tigrin.
pairs.question: Inter quae duo flumina regionem Mesopotamiam sitam esse Plinius tradit?
pairs.question_en: Between which two rivers does Pliny say the region of Mesopotamia lies?
pairs.answer_en: Between the Euphrates and the Tigris.
pairs.derivation: Mesopotamia lies between the Euphrates and the Tigris. Anchored to the named region; two-river answer supported verbatim by Mesopotamia inter Euphraten et Tigrin. Indirect statement (Mesopotamiam sitam esse) governed by tradit; closed-book (the very meaning of 'Mesopotamia').

pairs.source_text: in qua fuere Hierosolyma, longe clarissima urbium orientis, non Iudaeae modo.
pairs.question: Quae urbs Iudaeae a Plinio 'longe clarissima urbium orientis' appellatur?
pairs.question_en: Which city of Judaea does Pliny call 'by far the most famous of the cities of the East'?
pairs.derivation: Pliny's superlative for Jerusalem, longe clarissima urbium orientis. Anchored to Judaea; single-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book and iconic; passive appellatur keeps the 'according to Pliny' frame.

pairs.source_text: Ab occidente litora Esseni fugiunt usque qua nocent, gens sola et in toto orbe praeter ceteras mira, sine ulla femina, omni venere abdicata, sine pecunia, socia palmarum.
pairs.question: Quae gens ad occidentale latus lacus Asphaltitae sine ulla femina degere a Plinio traditur?
pairs.question_en: Which people does Pliny record as living on the western side of the Dead Sea (Lake Asphaltites) without any woman?
pairs.derivation: Pliny's famous notice placing the celibate Esseni on the western shore of the Dead Sea. Anchored to the lake + the womanless people; single named-people answer supported verbatim by Esseni ... sine ulla femina. Nominativus cum infinitivo governed by traditur; closed-book (the Essenes).

pairs.source_text: Tyros, quondam insula praealto mari DCC passibus divisa, nunc vero Alexandri oppugnantis operibus continens; olim partu clara, urbibus genitis Lepti, Utica et illa aemula terrarumque orbis avida Carthagine, etiam Gadibus extra orbem conditis.
pairs.question: Cuius urbis Phoeniciae partu Carthaginem, Uticam, Gades genitas esse Plinius tradit?
pairs.question_en: By the offspring of which Phoenician city does Pliny say Carthage, Utica, and Gades were founded?
pairs.derivation: Tyre as the Phoenician mother-city of Carthage (and Utica and Gades). Anchored to Carthage et al.; single-name answer (genitive) supported verbatim by Tyros ... urbibus genitis ... Carthagine ... Gadibus. Indirect statement governed by tradit; closed-book (Carthage's Tyrian foundation).

pairs.source_text: Arabia supra dicta habet oppida Edessam, quae quondam Antiochia dicebatur, Callirhoem, a fonte nominatam, Carrhas, Crassi clade nobile.
pairs.question: Quod oppidum a Plinio 'Crassi clade nobile' dicitur?
pairs.question_en: Which town does Pliny call 'famous for the defeat of Crassus'?
pairs.derivation: Carrhae as the site famous for Crassus' disaster. Anchored to Crassus; single-name answer supported verbatim by Carrhas, Crassi clade nobile. Closed-book and iconic (the Battle of Carrhae, 53 BC).

pairs.source_text: Palmyra, urbs nobilis situ, divitiis soli et aquis amoenis, vasto undique ambitu haernis includit agros ac, velut terris exempta a rerum natura, privata sorte inter duo imperia summa Romanorum Parthorumque est, prima in discordia semper utrimque cura.
pairs.question: Inter quae duo summa imperia urbem Palmyram sitam esse Plinius scribit?
pairs.question_en: Between which two great empires does Pliny say the city of Palmyra is situated?
pairs.answer_en: Between the empires of the Romans and the Parthians.
pairs.derivation: Palmyra lies between the two great empires of Rome and Parthia. Anchored to the named city; two-empire answer supported verbatim by inter duo imperia summa Romanorum Parthorumque est. Indirect statement (Palmyram sitam esse) governed by scribit; closed-book and recognizable.

pairs.source_text: Sed pulcherrima est libera Rhodos, circuitu CXXV aut, si potius Isidoro credimus, CIII, habitata urbibus Lindo, Camiro, Ialyso, nunc Rhodo.
pairs.question: Quam insulam, urbibus Lindo, Camiro, Ialyso habitatam, Plinius pulcherrimam liberamque esse tradit?
pairs.question_en: Which island, inhabited by the cities Lindus, Camirus, and Ialysus, does Pliny say is the most beautiful and free?
pairs.derivation: Pliny's superlative for Rhodes (pulcherrima ... libera), with its three classic cities. Anchored to Lindus/Camirus/Ialysus; single-name answer supported verbatim. Indirect statement (insulam pulcherrimam esse) governed by tradit; closed-book and iconic.
